Triage: promoted `pm:queue`, type Task. A build that prints TS2353 and exits 0 lies to anyone branching on its exit code mid-task; CI's separate `type-check` leg keeps this from shipping breakage, which caps severity at Task. Landing point: fail-on-error in the shared vite/dts config once (width-check the packages sharing the shape); if the leniency turns out deliberate, the deliverable is the comment saying so at the config site — the dev may surface that call in the PR rather than pre-asking.

## Premise correction: this repo has no shared vite/dts config, so "wire it once" was not achievable as stated

PM round 21, session `session_01RV6yuVCxymHYE16PL9vQkE`. Recording on the card because the correction lands on **triage's stated landing point**, not on the defect.

Triage graded this with: *"Landing point: fail-on-error in the shared vite/dts config once."* Measured by the dev on `origin/main` `478ec54ce`:

- **22 packages** build typings through `vite-plugin-dts`, and **each calls `dts()` in its own `vite.config.ts`**.
- The only shared dts module — `scripts/vite-dts-explicit-extensions.ts`, landed today by #5365 — is imported by exactly **2** of them.

So there is no single config to wire. A shared factory reaches only what a call site spreads it into. The dev implemented the factory once, wired one call site (`packages/layout`, the package the card measured), and filed the 20-package rollout as **#5483** — marking the PR `Part of #5370` rather than `Fixes`, so merging does not close a card that is one-of-22 deep. ⛔ I am leaving it that way: closing at 1/22 would misreport it.

### The defect is 21 packages wide, and the one exception is an accident

With a deliberate `TS2322` injected into each package's entry file, the exit codes are:

| packages | exit | why |
|---|---:|---|
| `@object-ui/layout` | **1** | wired by PR #5482 |
| `@object-ui/fields` | **2** | honest, but **by a different mechanism** — its build script is `tsc && vite build && …`, so the leading `tsc` fails first and the dts leg never runs |
| the other **20** | **0** | print the error, exit 0 |

`fields` being safe is a property of its script ordering, not of the dts leg. Worth knowing before anyone reads "21 of 22" as "one package already fixed correctly".

**Blast radius is measured zero**: on unmodified `main`, 22/22 build with no diagnostics of any category, so making dts errors fatal reds nothing green today. ⚠️ And every one of those 22 zeros was counter-probed — the injected-`TS2322` sweep above **is** the counter-probe, and all 22 reported it, so no zero is the vacuous kind where a package's dts program never looked at its own `src`.

Method note worth keeping: the dev's **first** sweep silently missed the injected error, because `vite-plugin-dts` **colours the word `error`** and the detector was matching un-stripped output. It caught its own probe being fooled and re-ran with ANSI stripped. A counter-probe that catches a broken probe is the only kind that is worth anything.

### Fold-or-serial for the remainder — flagged, not answered

⛔ Not answering this one myself. **#5483** (this card's rollout, 20 `vite.config.ts` files) and **#5439** (`pm:queue`, 13 vite-built packages shipping extensionless typings — the *other* shared dts module) touch a heavily overlapping set of the same config files. The dev recommends bundling them.

That is a fold-or-serial call, and it belongs to triage unless triage assigns it to the dispatching seat. #5483 is currently unlabelled and awaiting first-touch grading; I am recording the overlap here and on #5483 so the grading has it, rather than deciding it in a dispatch order. *(I overrode a triage fold-or-serial answer earlier today without having read it — see #5382 — and this is the corrected practice.)*

The dev also proposes a ratchet so a new `vite-plugin-dts` package cannot land unwired, and correctly says **not yet**: today it would need an allowlist of 21 unwired packages, i.e. a ratchet that starts out mostly debt. After the rollout the allowlist is empty and the gate is a one-line assertion. Recorded as step 2 in #5483.

## Mechanism landed; the rollout is carried by #5483. Closing this card.

PM round 21, session `session_01RV6yuVCxymHYE16PL9vQkE`.

PR #5482 merged as `Part of #5370`: the fail-on-error factory exists, is pinned by a test, and is wired into `@object-ui/layout` — the package this card measured. The remaining 20 `vite-plugin-dts` packages each need a one-line spread in their own `vite.config.ts`, and the dev filed that as **#5483** with the full per-package exit-code table, the measured-zero blast radius, and the keep-it-wired gate as step 2.

The dev offered the bookkeeping choice explicitly: *"Flip it to `Fixes` if you prefer #5483 to carry the remainder."* Taking that option — one open card per unit of remaining work beats two cards for one job.

⚠️ **This is bookkeeping, not a judgement that the work is done.** 20 packages still print a type error and exit 0. If you would rather this card stay open as the umbrella, reopening is free.

Recorded so the next reader does not have to reconstruct it: the defect is **21 packages wide**, and the one apparent exception is an accident — `@object-ui/fields` is honest only because its build script is `tsc && vite build`, so the leading `tsc` fails first and the dts leg never runs.
